coverage.main: Read all seventeen pages of arXiv 1802.08686v2 (NeurIPS 2018): Sections 1-6 including Theorem 3 on transferability (Section 4.2), Tables 1-2, appendices A-B (proofs, checkerboard Figure 3) and C (model details, numerical bound evaluation Algorithm 1, generated-image Figures 4-5).
coverage.supplement: Appendices are embedded in the arXiv PDF and read. No separate NeurIPS supplement was retrieved.
coverage.excluded_results: Theorem 3 proves the existence of shared perturbations for two low-risk classifiers but reports no empirical transfer rate. Tables 1-2 compare per-classifier empirical minimal-perturbation robustness (DeepFool-style, in-distribution and unconstrained) with the paper's upper bounds on SVHN and CIFAR-10 generated data; each classifier is attacked directly. Figures 4-5 are illustrations.

f1.evidence: Error rates are reported per classifier (positive setup evidence), but there is no source/target transfer evaluation to which the field applies.

f2.evidence: Robustness is measured by label change on generated samples without ground truth (footnote 9); no transfer denominator exists.

f4.evidence: Reported quantities are robustness percentiles, not transfer proportions.

f5.evidence: Minimal-norm L2 robustness is measured rather than a fixed-budget transfer attack; no transfer result exists.

f6.evidence: No original transfer configuration exists for which a release could be sufficient or insufficient; the paper links only third-party architecture code.

artifact_checks.result: Downloaded and hashed v2; the paper links third-party DCGAN, pytorch-cifar and wide-residual-networks implementations and no authors' release. Not evaluated as a transfer artifact.

bounds_exclusion.reason: No empirical transfer misclassification rate is reported.

limitations: Retained in the frozen corpus with non-applicability reasons; a theoretical transferability result is not coded as missing reporting.
